name: Kavieng
note: Town: capital of New Ireland Province at the northern tip of the island, the main air and sea gateway and base for diving, surfing, fishing and island boat trips; WWII bombing and occupation history.

name: Namatanai
coordinates_source: OSM place=town "Namatanai" (photon); Wikivoyage geo tag -3.067,152.433 is about 67 km off and not used
note: Town: small town two-thirds of the way down New Ireland, the southern end of the Boluminski Highway and base for the Namatanai district and Tabar and Tigak trips.

name: Boluminski Highway
note: Road: the main highway down the east coast of New Ireland from Kavieng to Namatanai, a flat cycling route with inland waterholes such as Fissoa along it. A linear route, pinned at its midpoint.

name: New Hanover Island
note: Island: New Hanover (Lavongai), reached by boat from Kavieng, with the Three Island Harbour and eco-lodges; Kavieng dive sites lie between the town and the island.

name: Tabar Group
note: Island group: the Tabar islands off New Ireland (Tabar, Tatau, Simberi), reached by boat or domestic flight from Kavieng and offered on the Karanas Comfort Tours itinerary; remote with minimal tourist traffic.

name: Tatau Island
note: Island: Tatau, a small island of the Tabar Group east of New Ireland, near Simberi. Wikipedia only; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Lihir Group
note: Island group: Lihir, Mahur, Masahet and Sanambiet off the New Ireland coast, a gold-mining island group reached by scheduled flights from Namatanai; named as one of the province's islands, with little visitor infrastructure.

name: Tanga Islands
note: Island group: Tanga (Boang, Malendok, Lif and others) north-east of New Ireland, named in the province's island list and as a Karanas Comfort Tours area.

name: Feni Islands
note: Island group: the Feni (Anir) islands in the Bismarck Sea, named in the province's list of outer islands reached by boat from Kavieng.

name: Tsoi Islands
note: Island group: the Tsoi islands of New Ireland, named on the PNG tourism page (a photo caption and the Karanas Comfort Tours itinerary); no Wikipedia article under this name.

name: Djaul Island
note: Island: Djaul (Dyaul), an island in the Tigak/Djaul group off New Ireland. Its Wikipedia title is a disambiguation page and no visitor source names it as somewhere to go.

name: Nusa Island
coordinates_source: OSM place=island "Nusa Island" (photon; island node, centroid)
note: Island: small island five minutes by boat from Kavieng, home to the Nusa Island Retreat resort; named for its seafood buffet, swimming, diving and snorkelling. Mostly an accommodation venue.

name: Lissenung Island
note: Island: small island 20 minutes by boat from Kavieng with the Lissenung Island Resort, known for diving and a crab seafood platter; the resort is the draw, not a separate attraction.

name: Laraibina Eel Sanctuary
note: Wildlife: a sanctuary where visitors meet the revered resident eels, named as an eco-tour stop on the PNG tourism page; no Wikipedia article.

name: Fissoa
note: Waterholes: inland waterholes (Fissoa and others) along the Boluminski Highway, named on the PNG tourism page as a stop to explore; no Wikipedia article.

name: Deep Pete Wreck
note: Dive site: the WWII Mitsubishi F1M seaplane wreck known as Deep Pete, off Kavieng, named as a wreck dive on the PNG tourism page; no Wikipedia article.

name: Borpop Airfield
note: WWII site: remains of the Japanese-built Borpop (Huris) Airfield near Namatanai, one of the province's WWII airfields and bunkers named on the PNG tourism page; little is left visible.

name: Kavieng Rights Surf Break
note: Surf break: exposed reef break at Kavieng with consistent swell from November to April, for intermediate and advanced surfers; surf-forecast page, not a visitor guide.

name: Malagan Carvings
note: Culture: the Malagan carving tradition of New Ireland, seen in carving workshops and collections and at Malagan ceremonies; a practice rather than one fixed place, so the judge may fold it into the carving villages.

name: Libba Village
note: Village: Libba in northern New Ireland, a Malagan carving village named by a source as home to contemporary carver Ben Sisia; no visitor source describes visiting.

name: Lelet Plateau
note: Plateau: the Lelet Plateau in northern New Ireland, a Malagan carving area; a museum/art source names it, no visitor source and no Wikipedia article found.

name: Lorengau
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Lorengau geo tag (town centre; a town, not an attraction)
note: Town: capital of Manus Province on the edge of Seeadler Harbour, with a market, a garamut dance tradition, sago village visits and the Harbourside Hotel tours.

name: Manus Island
note: Island: the main island of the Admiralty group, where Lorengau, Seeadler Harbour and the WWII sites are; the province is named for it.

name: Los Negros Island
note: Island: Los Negros, linked to Lorengau by causeway, with Momote Airport and the WWII Allied base sites; reached from Lorengau.

name: Momote Memorial Park
note: Memorial park: WWII memorial park at Momote on Los Negros, named on the Seeadler Bay Hotel listing on the PNG tourism page as one of Lorengau's attractions.

name: Seeadler Harbour
note: Harbour: the Seeadler Harbour (Seeadler Bay) at Lorengau, a WWII US naval base harbour with the Seeadler Bay Hotel and Harbourside Hotel on its shore; a water body visited by boat.

name: Lombrum Naval Base
note: WWII site: the Lombrum Point US naval base on Manus with rusting relics (per a travel article); no visitor-oriented source names it as a stop beyond that.

name: Pak Island
note: Island: Pak, an island of the Admiralty group in Manus Province. Wikipedia only; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Rambutyo Island
note: Island: Rambutyo (Rambutso), one of the Admiralty Islands in Manus Province. Wikipedia only; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Wuvulu Island
note: Island: Wuvulu, the westernmost of the Western Islands in Manus Province, with Aua and nearby atolls. Wikipedia only in this pass; no visitor source found.

name: Aua Island
note: Island: Aua, part of the Western Islands of Manus Province with Wuvulu. Wikipedia only in this pass; no visitor source found.

name: Tuluman Island
note: Island: small volcanic island that rose from the sea in the 1950s after an undersea eruption, named on the PNG tourism page as a Manus excursion; no Wikipedia article under this name.

name: Koruniat Island
note: Island: Koruniat Island in Seeadler Bay near Lorengau, named as one of the area's attractions on the Seeadler Bay Hotel listing on the PNG tourism page; no Wikipedia article.

name: Loniu Passage
note: Waterway: the Loniu Passage near Lorengau, named as one of the area's attractions on the Seeadler Bay Hotel listing on the PNG tourism page; a channel visited by boat.

name: Lou Island
note: Island: Lou Island in Manus Province, where obsidian was traditionally mined for tools, named on Wikivoyage Lorengau; the mining has largely died out.

name: Buka Island
note: Island: Buka Island, the arrival point for Bougainville by air and the Buka Passage boat trips; the island has the airport, the tourist office and most places to stay.

name: Buka
note: Town: Buka, the most bustling town in Bougainville and the seat of government since the civil war, with the Buka Market, the Buka Passage boats and waterfront restaurants.

name: Buka Passage
note: Waterway: the narrow strait between Buka Island and main Bougainville, visited by boat to the small islands and atolls, with Sohano the most-visited stop.

name: Sohano Island
coordinates_source: OSM place=village "Sohano" (photon; the village node on the island)
note: Island: Sohano, the most visited island in the Buka Passage, with simple eateries and places to stay, a Japanese war memorial and plane wreck on its northern tip and a short K2 boat ride from Buka.

name: Tchibo Rock
note: Rock: a rock at the northern tip of Sohano Island, said by local legend to have magical properties; a small sight on the Buka Passage trip.

name: Buka Market
note: Market: the Buka Market, where handicrafts and fish-on-a-stick are sold; a daily market in Buka town.

name: Arawa
note: Town: Arawa, the former administrative capital and centre of the Panguna copper mining business, partly derelict since the war, which Wikivoyage counts as one entity with Kieta.

name: Kieta
note: Port town: Kieta on the east coast beside Arawa, a port with few inhabitants since the conflict, known mainly for its transport links.

name: Kokopau
note: Village: Kokopau, the arrival point on the main island after crossing from Buka, the start of the scenic coast road south through villages such as Tinputz.

name: Tinputz
note: Village: Tinputz, a coastal village at the north-eastern point of Bougainville on the scenic coast road from Kokopau.

name: Panguna Mine
coordinates_source: OSM landuse=quarry "Panguna open pit" (photon; the pit, a visitor-restricted point)
note: Mine: the disused Panguna copper mine, one of the largest man-made holes on earth, inside a no-go zone; Wikivoyage says it is reached only with a well-connected local. Restricted access.

name: Morgan Junction
note: Town: Morgan Junction, the old gateway town to the Panguna mine, with barricades marking the no-go zone; Wikivoyage lists it as a civil-war site to respect, not a stop.

name: Wakunai
note: Village: Wakunai on the east coast, the start of the Mount Balbi treks and the place to buy Bougainville's renowned basket-ware.

name: Mount Balbi
note: Mountain: Mount Balbi (2,715 m), an active volcano in the Emperor Range, the highest in the Bougainville chain, reached by a three-day trek from Wakunai.

name: Emperor Range
note: Mountain range: the Emperor Range, which holds Mount Balbi, Billy Mitchell and the crossing to the west coast; the trekking area, not a single stop.

name: Mount Bagana
note: Volcano: Mount Bagana, a very active volcano in south-central Bougainville, visible from Mount Balbi; seen from trekking routes, not a regular visitor stop.

name: Mount Billy Mitchell
note: Volcano: dormant volcano in the Emperor Range with a 2 km wide caldera lake, reached on the Balbi trek extension.

name: Yamamoto Bomber Wreck
note: WWII site: the Mitsubishi bomber wreck where Admiral Yamamoto was shot down on 18 April 1943, about 3 km off the east coast road south of Arawa, with a signpost; visible in the jungle.

name: Nissan Island
note: Island: Nissan (Green Island), about 100 km north of Buka, with an American WWII airstrip, relics and a guest house with no telephone booking.

name: Carteret Islands
note: Islands: the Tulun (Carteret) atolls about 100 km north-east of Buka, one to two metres above sea level and threatened by sea-level rise; no facilities for visitors.

name: Cape Torokina
note: WWII site: Cape Torokina on Bougainville's west coast, the 1 November 1943 US Marine landing zone; no visitor-oriented source found naming it as a stop.

name: Buin
note: Town: Buin on the southern tip of Bougainville, a former Japanese base with WWII relics and the wrecked Yamamoto bomber nearby; reached by the gravel track from Arawa.
